title: Đề thi thử VSTEP — Nghe (P1 B1 · P2 B2 · P3 B2/C1/C2)

questions.content:
listening — Part 1

What do they decide to give their mother?
options: A. A scarf from the sister and a cake from the brother
B. Only a chocolate cake
C. Only a silk scarf
D. A handbag and some flowers
questions.explanation: Let me get the scarf, and you order the cake. That way she gets both.

questions.content:
listening — Part 1

What does the speaker want her friend to help with?
options: A. Showing her parents around the city
B. Taking photographs of her family
C. Driving her parents to the park
D. Booking a table for dinner at a restaurant
questions.explanation: Could you help us take some pictures at the riverside park in the afternoon?

questions.content:
listening — Part 1

What does the mother offer to do?
options: A. Visit her child next weekend
B. Transfer money for a new jacket
C. Mail an additional blanket
D. Buy an umbrella and send it by post
questions.explanation: Do you need me to send you an extra blanket?

questions.content:
listening — Part 1

What is the advantage of the private school?
options: A. It is closer to the family's home
B. It charges no tuition fees
C. It provides free school meals
D. It has fewer students per class
questions.explanation: the classes are much smaller, only twenty students.

questions.content:
listening — Part 1

What do they agree to do?
options: A. Put money aside for another year before choosing
B. Buy an apartment with a loan immediately
C. Move to a cheaper rental apartment
D. Ask their parents for financial help
questions.explanation: Let's save for one more year, then decide.

questions.content:
listening — Part 1

According to the speaker, how can you make the melon less bitter?
options: A. Soak it in salt water for an hour
B. Take out the seeds from inside thoroughly
C. Boil it for more than thirty minutes
D. Peel off the green skin first
questions.explanation: remove all the seeds inside carefully. That will reduce the bitter taste.

questions.content:
listening — Part 1

What did the speaker help her grandmother with?
options: A. How to send a text message
B. How to download a new chat application
C. How to start a face-to-face call on the phone
D. How to change the phone's screen background
questions.explanation: she wanted to learn how to make video calls.

questions.content:
listening — Part 1

Why did the speaker go home last weekend?
options: A. To attend a family gathering for a holiday
B. To paint the walls of the family home
C. To help his dad move to a new house
D. To repair storm damage to his father's house
questions.explanation: I went back to my hometown to help my dad fix the roof. some of the tiles were broken, and water was leaking into the bedroom.

questions.content:
listening — Part 2

According to Grace, what should mainly guide your choice of backpack?
options: A. Its colour and how much it costs
B. The duration of the trip and your physical build
C. Whether it is the largest model on sale
D. The number of outside pockets it has
questions.explanation: Choose it for the length of the trip and for your body, not just for colour or price.

questions.content:
listening — Part 2

What capacity does she suggest is sufficient for a single-day outing?
options: A. Around thirty-five litres
B. Around fifty litres
C. Around seventy litres
D. More than one hundred litres
questions.explanation: For a day trip, about thirty-five litres and a few outside pockets are enough.

questions.content:
listening — Part 2

Why does she favour a firm base and separate inner sections?
options: A. They make the pack appear more costly
B. They guard your belongings and keep leaky items apart from clothes
C. They allow the pack to use fewer straps
D. They prevent people from carrying tools
questions.explanation:
A solid base helps prevent broken containers and crushed clothes.
creams or food can leak in hot weather, and you do not want them mixed with dry clothes.

questions.content:
listening — Part 2

What is the purpose of the air holes in the padded section?
options: A. To conceal valuable items
B. To make the pack resistant to water
C. To release sweat and keep you comfortable
D. To hold climbing gear in place
questions.explanation:
make sure the padded area has air holes.
Without them, sweat cannot escape, and even a short climb becomes uncomfortable.

questions.content:
listening — Part 2

What does Nora want as her birthday present?
options: A. A car of her own
B. Lessons to learn to drive
C. A part-time job at weekends
D. A celebration with friends
questions.explanation: I was hoping for driving lessons.

questions.content:
listening — Part 2

Why does her father hesitate about the idea?
options: A. He thinks she is not old enough yet
B. Her school does not allow it
C. The family has no car and the costs would be hard to cover
D. Nobody is willing to teach her
questions.explanation:
we do not own a car, and the practice is the expensive part.
Insurance alone can cost more than the lessons themselves.

questions.content:
listening — Part 2

How does Nora propose to handle the expense?
options: A. By asking to use her teacher's vehicle
B. By taking weekend work to contribute to the insurance
C. By selling the gifts she receives
D. By skipping the family dinner
questions.explanation: I could work on Saturdays and Sundays to pay part of it.

questions.content:
listening — Part 2

What do they agree on in the end?
options: A. She will purchase a car straight away
B. She will abandon the plan entirely
C. Her father will cover a single trial lesson, and they will eat out
D. She will start driving a taxi for the family
questions.explanation:
I can pay for one trial lesson so you know what it feels like
could we still go out to dinner so Mum does not have to cook?

questions.content:
listening — Part 2

What is the student's project mainly about?
options: A. How factories pollute the air
B. Why tropical forests are disappearing
C. The reasons behind climate change and ways to address it
D. Encouraging recycling in the neighborhood
questions.explanation: It focuses on climate change—specifically, the causes and possible solutions.

questions.content:
listening — Part 2

What does the teacher identify as the leading driver of climate change?
options: A. Naturally occurring disasters
B. Energy produced by burning coal, oil, and gas
C. Modern farming methods
D. Shifts in ocean currents
questions.explanation: The biggest contributor is the burning of fossil fuels, like coal, oil, and natural gas.

questions.content:
listening — Part 2

How does the teacher describe the role of natural events such as volcanic eruptions?
options: A. They are the primary force behind global warming.
B. Their influence is minor next to what people cause.
C. They are growing more harmful year after year.
D. Their effects persist far longer than human emissions.
questions.explanation:
but their impact is relatively small compared with what humans are doing
Volcanic eruptions, for instance, can release gases, but these effects are usually temporary.

questions.content:
listening — Part 2

What does the teacher suggest would make the student's presentation stronger?
options: A. Adding real-world examples of projects and campaigns
B. Presenting a smaller number of arguments
C. Dealing only with the topic of energy efficiency
D. Leaving out any mention of government action
questions.explanation:
Concrete examples show that solutions are practical, not just theoretical.
They also make your project more persuasive.

questions.content:
listening — Part 3

What is the speaker's main purpose?
options: A. To persuade all school leavers to avoid university
B. To challenge doubts and explain how apprenticeships work
C. To recruit apprentices for medicine and law
D. To warn parents about student debt at university

questions.content:
listening — Part 3

What does the speaker say apprentices gain from day one?
options: A. A recognised qualification only
B. Free university tuition
C. A real salary while they train
D. A guaranteed senior engineering post

questions.content:
listening — Part 3

How is the study day connected to the work?
options: A. Study happens only after the apprenticeship ends
B. Studying replaces four days of work
C. The two are kept deliberately separate
D. What is learned is applied in the same week

questions.content:
listening — Part 3

What does the speaker admit about apprenticeships?
options: A. They suit those aiming for careers like medicine less well
B. They always pay more than a graduate job
C. They leave apprentices with student debt
D. They offer no recognised qualification

questions.content:
listening — Part 3

What does the speaker imply about earnings over time?
options: A. Graduates always keep their early pay advantage
B. The early pay gap tends to narrow and may reverse
C. Apprentices never catch up with graduates
D. Apprentices earn more than graduates from day one

questions.content:
listening — Part 3

What central question does the lecture pursue?
options: A. How to achieve human immortality
B. Why machines wear out faster than bodies
C. How to reverse ageing in humans today
D. Why ageing occurs despite the body's powers of self-repair

questions.content:
listening — Part 3

Why does the speaker reject the machine analogy?
options: A. Because living bodies, unlike machines, repair themselves
B. Because machines age faster than living bodies
C. Because machines cannot reproduce
D. Because ageing does not involve any damage

questions.content:
listening — Part 3

According to the evolutionary explanation, why do late-acting harmful genes persist?
options: A. They improve reproduction directly
B. They are invisible to selection after reproduction
C. They are too rare to matter
D. They are actively favoured by the body

questions.content:
listening — Part 3

What is the speaker's attitude toward claims that ageing will soon be abolished?
options: A. Enthusiastic endorsement
B. Complete indifference
C. Sober scepticism
D. Outright fatalism

questions.content:
listening — Part 3

What does the speaker suggest biology realistically offers?
options: A. Indefinite youth for humans
B. Proof that nothing can be done about ageing
C. A cure for all age-related disease within a decade
D. Compressing the years of frailty for a better late life

questions.content:
listening — Part 3

What is the speaker's overarching aim?
options: A. To prove that James's theory was entirely mistaken
B. To defend the common-sense sequence of perception, feeling, then bodily response
C. To catalogue the physical symptoms of fear
D. To trace the emotion debate and argue for a synthesis of bodily and interpretive accounts

questions.content:
listening — Part 3

James's "startling inversion" amounts to the claim that:
options: A. the feeling of an emotion is our perception of bodily changes that come first
B. emotions are simply cognitive judgements with no bodily component
C. the racing heart follows from the feeling of fear
D. fear and joy are physiologically indistinguishable

questions.content:
listening — Part 3

The observation that different emotions share similar physiology is used to argue that:
options: A. the body plays no role whatsoever in emotion
B. bodily feedback alone cannot determine which emotion a person is experiencing
C. James was entirely correct in his strong claim
D. appraisal is irrelevant to emotional experience

questions.content:
listening — Part 3

What is the speaker's attitude toward the idea that James was "simply refuted and superseded"?
options: A. Full agreement that appraisal theory replaced James completely
B. Indifference to whether James was right or wrong
C. Resistance, holding that James captured something enduringly correct
D. Insistence that appraisal theory has no merit

questions.content:
listening — Part 3

The speaker's preferred synthesis holds that:
options: A. appraisal alone constitutes an emotion, with the body irrelevant
B. the body alone determines the specific identity of each emotion
C. emotion is fully explained by the common-sense sequence
D. bodily arousal supplies raw intensity while interpretation confers a specific emotional identity
